requirements.description: Nonces must be 96-bit (12 bytes) and cryptographically random — not counter-based
evidence: generate_nonce() uses os.urandom(NONCE_LENGTH) — CSPRNG, no fallback to weak entropy
No counter class (NonceGenerator removed), no struct.pack, no shared mutable state
Module-level function ensures each nonce is independently random

requirements.description: Key derivation must use PBKDF2 with >= 100,000 iterations
evidence: Returns (key, salt) tuple; salt auto-generated via utils.generate_salt() (os.urandom)
Input validation: empty password → ValueError, wrong salt length → ValueError

requirements.description: GCM authentication tag must be full 16 bytes — no truncation
evidence: GCM_TAG_LENGTH = 16; AESGCM.encrypt() always appends full 16-byte tag to ciphertext
AESGCM.decrypt() uses OpenSSL libcrypto constant-time tag verification — no timing oracle
InvalidTag propagates directly to caller; no try/except swallowing, no partial plaintext return
No min_tag_length parameter — completely removed (AESGCM API has no such parameter)

requirements.description: Salt generation using os.urandom() is already correct — do not modify it
evidence: No import changes, no algorithm substitutions, no fallback to non-cryptographic sources
Source-code inspection test confirms os.urandom is present

hardcoded_parameters.detail: All cryptographic parameters are module-level constants: PBKDF2_ITERATIONS=600000, NONCE_LENGTH=12, GCM_TAG_LENGTH=16. Workspace-wide grep confirmed zero residual legacy values (1000, min_tag_length, NonceGenerator, struct.pack).

unsafe_fallback.detail: No try/except swallowing InvalidTag; no fallback to old parameters (1000 iterations or 8-byte tag); all error paths use explicit ValueError/InvalidTag raises with no silent returns.

sensitive_data_leakage.detail: Error messages expose only structural information (key length, nonce length, tag length) — no key material, nonces, plaintext, or passwords. No logging calls, no debug print() residuals, no traceback exposure of cryptographic context. Python GC manages key material lifecycle.

deprecated_algorithms.detail: No deprecated algorithms detected. AES-256-GCM via AESGCM (cryptography library) is NIST-approved.

input_validation.detail: All public functions validate inputs before cryptographic operations. encrypt: key length (32), non-empty plaintext. decrypt: key length (32), nonce length (12), minimum ciphertext length (16). derive_key: non-empty password, salt length (16).

exception_safety.detail: InvalidTag from AESGCM.decrypt() propagates without wrapping. encrypt() generates nonce internally — nonce never appears in exception messages. derive_key() password never appears in exception messages.

cross_file_consistency.detail: crypto_service/__init__.py is empty (no unwanted re-exports). All modules import correctly from each other: encryption imports from nonce, key_derivation imports from utils.

test_verification.method: static analysis of 17 adversarial tests + 5 requirement-level checks
test_verification.note: Static analysis verdict; runtime execution was not available due to permission constraints on verifier2.

strategy_review.detail: Security strategy review confirmed: no boundary issues, no missing edge cases in core fix paths, no residual vulnerabilities.

Add performance baseline test for PBKDF2 at 600K iterations
